documents.title: H&P - Admission - Sepsis, Urinary Source
lines: CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Fever and chills, low urine output x 1 day.
HPI:
85 yo male brought to ED by son at 02:10 with 1 day of chills, dysuria, lower abdominal discomfort, and decreased oral intake.
Reports urinary frequency and foul-smelling urine x 3 days. No cough, no chest pain, no vomiting, no diarrhea.
No recent hospitalization. No indwelling catheter. Lives at home with wife, independent in ADLs.
PMH:
Hypertension. BPH. Type 2 diabetes, diet controlled. CKD not documented, prior baseline creatinine 0.9 mg/dL.
Remote cholecystectomy. No known cardiac disease.
HOME MEDS:
Amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly.
Aspirin 81 mg daily.
Acetaminophen 650 mg PRN.
ALLERGIES: Penicillin - pt reports rash in childhood, tolerated cephalosporins since. No anaphylaxis.
SOCIAL: Former smoker, quit ~30 yrs ago. No alcohol. No illicit drugs.
FAMILY HX: Noncontributory.
ROS: Fever, chills, dysuria, fatigue. Denies headache, sore throat, dyspnea, rash, joint pain.
TRIAGE VITALS:
Temperature 37.9 C at triage, HR 118, BP 84/50, RR 22, SpO2 95% on RA.
Respiratory rate 22; SpO2 95% on RA, no oxygen needed.
EXAM:
Gen: Elderly male, ill appearing, diaphoretic, alert and answering questions appropriately.
HEENT: Dry mucous membranes. No scleral icterus.
Neck: Supple, no JVD.
Cardiac: Tachycardic, regular, no murmur.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles or wheeze, unlabored.
Abd: Soft, mild suprapubic tenderness, no guarding, no rebound. No CVA tenderness.
GU: No scrotal swelling. Prostate not examined.
Ext: Warm, no edema, cap refill 3 sec.
Skin: No rash, no cellulitis, no decubitus.
Neuro: Moves all extremities, follows commands, speech fluent.
LABS/STUDIES:
Lactate 2.1 mmol/L at 02:10, not repeated.
WBC 11,200 with 88% neutrophils.
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Na 134, K 4.6, HCO3 19, BUN 42, glucose 168. Total bili 1.1, INR 1.2.
Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field.
Blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
CXR portable: no consolidation, no effusion.
ED COURSE:
Received 1 L normal saline bolus; BP after bolus 102/64, MAP 77.
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added for empiric gram positive coverage pending cultures.
Vitals at 04:45 after fluids: HR 102, BP 104/62, RR 20.
Norepinephrine started at 04:50 at 0.05 mcg/kg/min, titrated to 0.12 mcg/kg/min to keep MAP above 65.
Right IJ not required; pressor running via well-placed 18 g antecubital with frequent site checks.
ASSESSMENT:
85 yo male with sepsis, likely urinary source, with vasopressor requirement, AKI on normal baseline renal function, and thrombocytopenia.
PLAN:
1. Sepsis - continue IV antibiotics, follow cultures and sensitivities, de-escalate when speciated.
2. Hemodynamics - titrate norepinephrine to MAP goal above 65, additional 500 mL NS boluses PRN, hourly MAP documentation.
3. AKI - hold amlodipine, strict I/O, foley placed for accurate output, renally dose meds, avoid NSAIDs and contrast.
4. Thrombocytopenia - repeat CBC q12h, transfusion threshold per attending, no heparin gtt.
5. Resp - monitor RR and SpO2, no supplemental O2 required.
6. Glucose - SSI moderate scale q6h.
7. Admit to stepdown telemetry. Full code confirmed with pt and son at bedside. Attending notified 05:10.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: SUBJECTIVE:
Pt reports feeling better, chills resolved, dysuria improved. Ate half of breakfast. No dyspnea, no chest pain.
Overnight: no fevers after 03:00. Urine output 40-60 mL/hr since foley.
OBJECTIVE:
Tmax 37.8 C, T now 36.9 C. HR 88, BP 112/66, MAP 81, RR 18, SpO2 96% on RA.
Norepinephrine weaned from 0.12 mcg/kg/min to 0.03 mcg/kg/min over the night for MAP above 65.
Exam: comfortable, mucous membranes moist, lungs clear, abd soft with minimal suprapubic tenderness, extremities warm.
LABS AM:
WBC 9,400. Platelets 96,000. Creatinine 1.9 mg/dL, BUN 34, HCO3 22.
Original values for reference: WBC 11,200; Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Blood and urine cultures pending final speciation.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Sepsis, urinary source - improving. Continue piperacillin-tazobactam and vancomycin pending culture data.
2. Shock - continue to wean norepinephrine, goal off by afternoon if MAP holds.
3. AKI - creatinine trending down with volume repletion, continue maintenance IVF at 75 mL/hr, amlodipine remains on hold.
4. Thrombocytopenia - platelets rising, recheck this evening.
5. Resp - no oxygen requirement, RR stable.
6. Mobility - out of bed to chair with PT today, DVT ppx with SCDs given platelet count.
Discussed course with son by phone 08:05.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: INTERVAL EVENTS:
Norepinephrine discontinued at 12:15 after taper; MAP maintained 78-88 off pressor for 3 hours.
Foley removed 13:00, voided 250 mL spontaneously at 14:40.
Micro called at 13:30: blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours; urine culture with greater than 100,000 CFU/mL gram negative rods.
Vancomycin discontinued per micro result. Antibiotic coverage narrowed discussion with attending - continue pip-tazo pending sensitivities.
VITALS:
T 36.8 C, HR 84, BP 118/70, MAP 86, RR 18, SpO2 97% on RA.
EXAM:
Sitting up in chair, no distress. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. No CVA tenderness. Extremities warm, no edema.
LABS PM:
Platelets 118,000. Creatinine 1.5 mg/dL. Lactate not repeated.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. E. coli bacteremia with urinary source - source controlled, off vasopressors, afebrile.
2. Continue IV antibiotics, plan to maintain IV route through day 3 before considering oral step down per sensitivities.
3. AKI - improving, continue oral intake, recheck BMP in AM at receiving unit.
4. Thrombocytopenia - resolving, no bleeding.
5. Transfer out of stepdown and discharge from this service to general medicine care tonight; sign-out completed 16:10.
6. Pt and wife updated at bedside 15:55, questions answered.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Sepsis Secondary to E. coli UTI
lines: ADMIT HD1, DISCHARGED FROM SERVICE HD2.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Sepsis with vasopressor requirement, urinary source.
2. E. coli bacteremia.
3. Acute kidney injury, resolving.
4. Thrombocytopenia, resolving.
BRIEF HOSPITAL COURSE:
85 yo male presented at 02:10 with fever, chills and dysuria. Temperature 37.9 C at triage; WBC 11,200.
Lactate 2.1 mmol/L at 02:10, not repeated. Respiratory rate 22; SpO2 95% on RA, no oxygen needed.
Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added; remained on IV antibiotics through day 3.
Received 1 L normal saline bolus; BP after bolus 102/64, MAP 77.
Vitals at 04:45 after fluids: HR 102, BP 104/62, RR 20.
Norepinephrine started at 04:50 at 0.05 mcg/kg/min, titrated to 0.12 mcg/kg/min to keep MAP above 65. Weaned off at 12:15 on HD2.
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000 on admission; creatinine 1.5 mg/dL and platelets 118,000 at discharge.
Blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours; vancomycin stopped once gram negative organism identified.
Foley placed for output monitoring, removed HD2 with successful spontaneous void.
DISCHARGE VITALS: T 36.8 C, HR 84, BP 118/70, RR 18, SpO2 97% on RA.
DISCHARGE EXAM: Ambulating with PT, lungs clear, abd soft nontender, no edema.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Continue IV antibiotic course as ordered through day 3, then oral agent per final sensitivities.
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly - resume.
Aspirin 81 mg daily - resume.
Amlodipine 5 mg daily - HOLD until BP and creatinine rechecked.
Acetaminophen 650 mg q6h PRN.
FOLLOW UP:
Repeat BMP and CBC in 3 days.
Primary care follow up within 1 week for BP recheck and decision on restarting amlodipine.
Urology follow up for BPH and recurrent UTI evaluation.
RETURN PRECAUTIONS: fever above 38.0 C, chills, inability to urinate, flank pain, lightheadedness, decreased oral intake.
Instructions reviewed with pt and wife, teach-back completed. Son notified by phone.
